Operations brief · Full period

Start with Rio de Janeiro

São Paulo had the highest late-order count. Rio combined a large number of missed promises with more frequent and longer delays.

Where to investigate

São Paulo had 1,817 late orders out of 40,399 (4.50%). Rio had 1,495 out of 12,310 (12.14%). Late orders in Rio averaged 13.5 days past promise, compared with 8.3 in São Paulo.

When to investigate

March 2018 was the worst purchase cohort. Of 7,003 orders, 1,328 arrived late (18.96%), versus 6.79% across the full period. Compare those shipments with adjacent months before attributing the spike to a carrier.

What to do next

Review Rio shipments by origin, service level and carrier scan history. As a planning scenario, reducing Rio’s late rate by one percentage point across the same volume would mean about 123 fewer late orders. Actual improvement needs a measured pilot.

Method and evidence

One order counts once. The denominator is delivered orders with a valid purchase, receipt, estimate and destination. Delivery on the promised calendar date counts as on time. Filters use purchase month and customer destination state.

Of 99,441 source orders, 99,092 fell in the purchase window. The analysis excludes 2,881 non-delivered orders and 8 delivered records that failed eligibility checks. Stage averages use 96,018 orders with a handoff between purchase and receipt. The source provides no carrier identity or service-level contract. The final purchase months may underrepresent unresolved orders.
